sections.content: How many people are "leisure and sports managers and proprietors"?

67,415 people

were counted on the census as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Leisure and sports managers and proprietors direct and co-ordinate the activities and resources required for the provision of sporting, artistic, theatrical and other recreational and amenity services.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors", 14.5% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" included:

  • betting shop and gambling establishment managers
  • dispensing opticians
  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" there were more men than women (60.4% compared with 39.6%).

This means "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "other managers and proprietors".

Men made up 60.4% and women made up 39.6% of "leisure and sports managers and proprietors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" included:

  • transport and distribution clerks and assistants
  • other elementary services occupations
  • purchasing managers and directors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "leisure and sports managers and proprietors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "leisure and sports managers and proprietors", 8.3% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (71.5% compared with 28.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (70.5%) than self-employed (29.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Buckinghamshire, this is in the same region of the South East.
